body.statement: On every weak-order cell \(\omega\in\Omega(p^{1:L})\), \[S(q)=\bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma_K}S_{(\omega,\sigma)}(q)=\bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma_K}\{C_{(\omega,\sigma)}x:A_{(\omega,\sigma)}x=b_{(\omega,\sigma)}+B_{(\omega,\sigma)}q,\ x\ge0\},\qquad |\Sigma_K|=\binom{2K-2}{K-1}.\] At a propensity--grid tie, adjacent order labels give duplicate boundary images, so the same bound holds for distinct images. Every feasible allocation is attained by one law satisfying the maintained model, and membership failure has one Farkas certificate for every path. Within the fixed finite outcome alphabet, the characterization remains valid when complier support is not full and supplies the joint policy set in that missing-support direction.
body.justification: The theorem identifies the entire simultaneous policy curve rather than separately sharp coordinates.
body.gap: Within the fixed finite outcome alphabet, Marx's Proposition 5 relies on full complier support; generic discrete instrumental-variable programs do not encode the common ordered rank across all latent-index bins.
body.consumer: Oregon Medicaid analysts can reject simultaneous discounted-take-up and never-treated extrapolations that pass every coordinatewise bound.
